text:
Mark Scheifele now stands alone as the Jets' all-time points leader, and he got there in the most Winnipeg way possible this month: four points and a shootout goal as the Jets erased a four-goal deficit in Chicago. The Winnipeg Free Press called it "another four-goal deficit," which tells you how this six-game winning streak has gone. Tonight is the first home crowd since the record, and the team's own video title sets it up plainly: "Scheifele Makes Franchise History as Ottawa Comes to Town."

The streak is not smoke. Winnipeg has outscored teams 32-18 across the six wins and taken 59% of the expected goals, the measure of chance quality, which is a sharper picture than a season line that still sits at 48% at five on five. Scheifele has a six-game point streak (5 goals, 9 assists), Kyle Connor has goals in three straight and just passed 700 career points, and Cole Perfetti has points in five straight. Dawson Mercer, ten games into life with a new team, scored twice in the 8-3 win in Dallas. Nino Niederreiter sits one point from 500.

Ottawa arrives with points in five straight (4-0-1) and the better five-on-five numbers this season, 53% of the expected goals. Linus Ullmark is the swing piece: .939 and 9.4 goals saved above expected in ten games, a season after finishing 13.3 below, and one win from 200 for his career. The Senators are short, though. William Eklund is on injured reserve with an ankle injury, Nick Cousins is out after a hit from Jakob Chychrun that drew headlines all week, and Hayden Hodgson and Warren Foegele are out too. The team's own video says Tyler Boucher, the 10th pick in 2021, is "Set For Emotional NHL Debut."

Watch the penalty box. Ottawa takes 4.6 penalties a game, and Winnipeg's power play creates 0.84 expected goals a game against a Senators kill that allows 0.80. Our numbers lean Ottawa on chances, 3.19 expected goals to 2.90.
headline: Scheifele's record night, Ottawa next through the door
